The Dangote Refinery is an oil refinery at Lekki, near Lagos, Nigeria, built by the businessman Aliko Dangote. It was commissioned in 2023 and began work in 2024. With a capacity of about 650,000 barrels a day, it is the world's largest single-train refinery, meaning one set of processing units.

It answers an old paradox. Nigeria has pumped oil since the find at Oloibiri in 1956 and is one of Africa's largest producers, yet it imported nearly all its petrol and diesel. Its state refineries had broken down, and a costly fuel subsidy rewarded importers.

Dangote, Africa's richest man, made his fortune in cement, sugar and flour. The refinery took years longer and cost far more than planned. It started with diesel and aviation fuel and began making petrol in September 2024. It has clashed with the state oil company and regulators over crude supply and fuel imports. The new Lekki Deep Sea Port lies nearby on the same coast.
